opening.argument: The instructions direct viewers to connect a MetaMask wallet, send liquidity to a newly created contract, and pay gas before running a flash-loan arbitrage bot. They require a deposit for execution—“You need to deposit at least 0.1 for the contract to execute correctly”—and promise that “The higher the liquidity, the higher the profit,” with profit returned within seconds or minutes. The frames corroborate that workflow: MetaMask requests wallet access, Remix presents a deployment and transaction interface, and a send form prepares an ETH transfer of 0.1 ETH. Yet the record does not establish that the code works, that the displayed balance resulted from the interaction, or that any profit was received.
